lines.cap: Cows swallow, then bring it back up for more.
lines.say: Cows swallow, then bring it back up for more.

lines.cap: A cow grabs mouthfuls of grass, and swallows them almost without chewing.
lines.say: A cow grabs mouthfuls of grass, and swallows them almost without chewing.

lines.cap: It lands in the rumen, the biggest of four stomach chambers. Big enough to hold a bathtub of food.
lines.say: It lands in the rumen, the biggest of four stomach chambers. Big enough to hold a bathtub of food.

lines.cap: Later, while resting, she brings small balls of it back up into her mouth. That's the cud.
lines.say: Later, while resting, she brings small balls of it back up into her mouth. That's the cud.

lines.cap: And she chews it again. Slowly. About forty to sixty times per mouthful.
lines.say: And she chews it again. Slowly. About forty to sixty times per mouthful.

lines.cap: Cows can spend up to eight hours a day chewing their cud.
lines.say: Cows can spend up to eight hours a day chewing their cud.

lines.cap: All that chewing breaks grass into tiny pieces, so microbes in the stomach can finish the job.
lines.say: All that chewing breaks grass into tiny pieces, so microbes in the stomach can finish the job.

lines.cap: So next time you see a cow chewing with nothing in front of her, she's having seconds.
lines.say: So next time you see a cow chewing with nothing in front of her, she's having seconds.
